a.verdict: pass, with no margin used at all

findings: Track A here is 1.0000 - not marginal, not close to the floor - while mac-bench measures 0.9849 and 0.9771 on the same commit
and the ORDERING is reversed: on this bench Track B is the one with a second populated bucket (0.9932) and Track A has none. On mac-bench Track A fails and Track B passes.
so it is not a pure property of the code at 49dd967 - the same commit gives opposite orderings on two benches
my_own_hypothesis_refuted: I suspected ctl_port_sof_poll(), which I added to Track A's loop: its edge branch calls micros() at 869 ns once per SOF frame, and I reasoned that at Track A's slower loop that would be ~1.3% of passes against a 1% allowance. Measured, Track A runs at 108,943 passes/s - not the ~75k I assumed - and 869 ns on a 9.2 us pass is 9%, nowhere near the doubling a log2 bucket needs. The arithmetic does not support it and the measurement does not either.
method_note: the suite FLASHES the board to match --track. Running the test without --track after manually uploading Track A silently measured Track B and reported a pass; the identity line is what caught it. Any per-track measurement here must pass --track or check `v` afterwards.
